License is PERMISSION, not transfer of interest in land. Distinguished from lease (which transfers interest). Cite Associated Hotels of India v. R.N. promptInstructions: Draft a LICENSE AGREEMENT under the Easements Act, 1882, Section 52.

S.52 Easements Act — LICENSE DEFINED: 'Where one person grants to another, or to a definite number of other persons, a right to do, or continue to do, in or upon the immovable property of the grantor, something which would, in the absence of such right, be unlawful, and such right does not amount to an easement or an interest in the property, the right is called a license.'

ESSENTIAL FEATURES OF LICENSE (distinguishes from lease):
   (a) PERMISSION — not transfer of any interest.
   (b) NO INTEREST IN LAND created.
   (c) PERSONAL to licensee — not transferable / heritable (by default).
   (d) REVOCABLE (S.60 Easements Act) — except where coupled with transfer of property OR where licensee has incurred expenses on faith of license (S.60 proviso).
   (e) LICENSOR RETAINS LEGAL POSSESSION AND CONTROL of premises.

CRITICAL DISTINCTION — LICENSE vs LEASE: Cite Associated Hotels of India Ltd v. R.N. Kapoor AIR 1959 SC 1262, and Khalil Ahmed Bashir Ahmed v. Tufelhussein Samasbhai (1988) 1 SCC 155. Test:
   (i) INTENTION of the parties.
   (ii) EXCLUSIVE POSSESSION — if grantee has exclusive possession (i.e., right to exclude even the grantor) — strong indicator of LEASE.
   (iii) Substance over form — labelling as 'license' is not conclusive if substance is lease.
   (iv) Right to make structural changes / sublease — indicators of lease.

If license language is overly lease-like (e.g., 'shall have exclusive possession for the term', 'transferable', 'fixed long term with renewal'), the courts and Stamp Authority MAY RE-CHARACTERISE as lease — exposing parties to (i) higher stamp duty, (ii) tenancy rights for licensee, (iii) registration mandate, (iv) Rent Control Act applicability.
DRAFTING PRINCIPLES to preserve LICENSE character:
- Use 'PERMISSION TO USE' language, NOT 'grants possession' or 'demises'.
- Explicitly state: 'No interest in land or any easement or tenancy is created.'
- Licensor retains keys / master access / right to inspect at any time.
- Licensee occupies as PERMITTEE, not as tenant.
- Where 'exclusive' use of a portion is given — frame as 'designated area for licensee's use; licensor retains right of access and inspection'.
- License is PERSONAL to licensee — non-transferable, non-assignable, non-heritable.
- REVOCABLE on notice or per terms; not a permanent right.
- License fee, not 'rent'; deposit, not 'security against tenancy'.
- Term typically short (11 months for leave-and-license following Maharashtra pattern); even for longer, no renewal at licensee's option without licensor consent.
STRUCTURE:
Para 1: Parties identification.

Para 2: Recital — Licensor is owner / authorised occupier of the premises described in Schedule A; Licensee has approached for permission to use the premises for the limited purpose of [specific purpose].

Para 3: Grant of License — 'Licensor doth hereby GRANT to the Licensee a BARE LICENSE under Section 52 of the Easements Act, 1882, to enter upon and use the portion described in Schedule A SOLELY for the purpose of [purpose], for a period of [months], commencing from [start date].'
Para 4: No Interest in Land — 'This is a personal license. No interest in land, no tenancy, no easement, and no proprietary right of any nature whatsoever is created in favour of the Licensee.'

Para 5: Licensor's Retained Possession — 'The Licensor shall at all times retain legal possession, control and dominion over the premises. The Licensee occupies and uses the premises as PERMITTEE / LICENSEE only, and not as tenant, lessee or any kind of holder of interest.'
Para 6: Purpose — narrowly defined; no other use without prior written consent.
Para 7: Term — [N] months from start date.
Para 8: License Fee — monthly, payable on or before [date]; mode (bank transfer); GST as applicable on commercial license.
Para 9: Security Deposit — refundable interest-free on vacating; deductions for damages / arrears.
Para 10: Non-Assignment — license is PERSONAL; cannot be transferred, sublicensed, assigned, or shared with any other person without prior written consent of Licensor.

Para 11: Licensee's Obligations:
   - Pay license fee timely.
   - Use only for permitted purpose.
   - Maintain premises in good condition; no structural alteration.
   - Comply with society rules, building regulations, local laws.
   - Bear electricity, water, internet, society maintenance as agreed.
   - Allow Licensor's inspection on reasonable notice.
   - Vacate immediately on termination; surrender keys and possession.

Para 12: Licensor's Obligations:
   - Ensure quiet use during license term, subject to licensor's retained rights.
   - Provide basic services as agreed (water, electricity, parking).

Para 13: Termination:
   (a) At end of term automatically.
   (b) Either party may terminate on [X] days' notice.
   (c) On material breach by licensee — immediate termination + forfeiture of deposit.
   (d) On material breach by licensor — licensee may vacate and recover deposit.

Para 14: Vacating: 'Upon termination by any cause, Licensee shall forthwith vacate and hand over peaceful possession of the premises; shall not claim any tenancy, occupancy, possessory or other right; the Licensor shall be entitled to re-enter without recourse to any proceeding for possession.'

Para 15: TDS — Licensee shall deduct TDS u/s 194-I (corporate licensee, fee > Rs.2.4L p.a.) or 194-IB (individual licensee, fee > Rs.50K p.m.) — even for license fee, courts have treated it as 'rent' for TDS purposes.

Para 16: GST — for commercial license (non-residential), GST applies @ 18% on license fee where licensor's turnover > GST threshold; reverse charge for unregistered licensors leasing to registered businesses (CGST Notification 5/2022).
Para 17: Indemnity — Licensee indemnifies Licensor for damage / liability arising from use; insurance coverage required for commercial licenses.
Para 18: Dispute Resolution — Arbitration under Arbitration & Conciliation Act 1996; or civil court jurisdiction at specified place.
Para 19: Governing Law — Indian law.

Para 20: STAMP DUTY — Article 5 / 35 of State Stamp Act (varies):
   - License is typically chargeable under 'Agreement' article OR specific 'Leave and License' article.
   - Where state has specific Leave and License article (e.g., Maharashtra Article 36A) — applies.
   - Bihar / Jharkhand / UP / Delhi: typically lower than lease — often Rs.100 to Rs.500 fixed OR small % for commercial.
   - VERIFY state schedule.

Para 21: REGISTRATION — license agreements are NOT compulsorily registerable under S.17 Registration Act (since no interest in land created). HOWEVER, some states (Maharashtra, Karnataka) mandate registration of leave-and-license. Bihar / Jharkhand / UP / Delhi do not mandate.
Schedule A — Licensed Premises description.
Two witnesses' attestation.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

WHERE LICENSEE INVESTS IN PREMISES on faith of license — flag S.60 proviso Easements Act: license becomes irrevocable to extent of investment unless terms expressly negative this. Include explicit clause that no investment / improvement creates any equity / right of irrevocability.
